data.answer:
The **2015 mining study** found that **publicly funded entities co-filed most often (21 per cent)**, while **METS firms co-filed least often (3.6 per cent)**.[1]

Collaboration was measured using patent applications with more than one applicant. These figures cover **PCT applications only**, so they are not a comprehensive measure of mining collaboration.[2]

citations.quote: METS firms collaborate the least (3.6 per cent) and publicly funded collaborate the most (21 per cent).

claims.text: The 2015 mining study found publicly funded entities co-filed most often, at 21 per cent, and METS firms least often, at 3.6 per cent.

citations.quote: collaboration was determined by looking at PCT applications with more than one applicant (or where applications include co-applicants) and their entity types. These results are based on the subset comprising PCT applications only so is not comprehensive

claims.text: Collaboration was measured through multiple-applicant patent applications, covering PCT applications only rather than all mining collaboration.
